items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 45:1
items.html: This is by reason of the inverse relation between vessels and lights. For all the deficiencies in the Partzuf, just as they touch the vessels in the lowest phase among them, so do they touch the lights in the highest phase among them: with the lack of the lowest vessel the highest light is therefore lacking, and if the two lowest vessels are lacking, this causes the lack of the two highest lights. Thus the lack of light in the vessel of Malchut shows that the light of Keter is lacking from the lights of the Partzuf, and so conversely. And the lack of light in the two lower vessels, ZA and Malchut, shows the lack of the two upper lights, Keter and Hochma, and so always. And the reason is simple: the clothing of the lights in vessels is measured by the coarseness in the screen that couples with the upper light. Therefore, when the screen rises from Malchut to ZA, which is phase three, and the coupling is made in phase three, Malchut remains without light, since the place of the coupling has risen to ZA; and the light of Keter is also lacking, since from a screen of the discernment of ZA only a level of Hochma emerges. And if the place of the coupling has risen to phase two, to Bina, then the vessel of ZA also remains without light, and you now have two lower vessels without light, and correspondingly the two upper lights, the light of Keter and the light of Hochma, will be lacking, for from the coupling made in the screen of phase two only a level of Bina emerges. And so always. (Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 8)
